chapter_title: Concerning the Three Blows that befell the Enemy because of the Light.
chapter_note: The chapter is essentially a compact, systematic eschatological teaching: a threefold sequence of defeats/bindings of the Enemy by the Light. Only the opening dialogue-attribution (“Once again he turned, and says:”) functions as late compilation frame; the rest stays cosmos→cosmos (wars, binding, dissolution in fire, final separation and confinement) without institutional/pastoral application.

paragraphs.core_text: The Darkness itself, the Enemy, has received three bad blows with three wars; and worse dangers from the Light in those three wars.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again he turned, and says:” (late compilation framing).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The content is core-like (impersonal cosmological statement of a threefold structure), but the introductory turn-and-says formula is a classic redactional dialogue frame marker; stripping it yields a self-standing teaching incipit.

paragraphs.core_text: The first: (The Enemy) was brought out to the middle and separated from his dark earth, whence he had departed. He was vanquished in that first war, caught and [bound] by the Living Soul.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic numbered sequence (“The first”) describing what happened in cosmic war and binding; all referents are internal to the Manichaean cosmological drama (Enemy, dark earth, Living Soul), with no application voice.

paragraphs.core_text: The second blow is the time when he will be dissolved and melted, and he perishes in this great fire. He is destroyed and overthrown, from the images that are all by which he exists. And he will be gathered in [to the] fetter corresponding to his archetype, and be made like he was from the first beginning.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological process-description (dissolution, melting, perishing in great fire; regathering into a fetter ‘corresponding to his archetype’) remains within a closed cosmic mechanism—typical of the older expository substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The third blow that will befall the Enemy is the 'rolling back' [at the] end when everything will be separated, and male will be divided [from] female. Now, the male will be bound in the lump, but the female [will be thrown] in to the tomb. For it will be divided [ ... by a great] stone in their midst, for generation upon generation, for ever and ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still impersonal and structural: final separation (‘rolling back’), gendered division, lump/tomb confinement, great stone barrier. No institutional identification or exhortation; the imagery functions as cosmic eschatology, not social pointing.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the way that the binding of the Enemy will come about, in a fetter that is burdensome and strong, one from which there is never escape; because [they have achieved] his binding and bound him for ever. And they have achieved his being set apart, and he has been set apart for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summative closure of the mechanism (binding in an inescapable fetter; permanent set-apartness) stays within the cosmic system and lacks second-person address; the repetitive finality reads as doctrinal exposition rather than pastoral enforcement.
